summary: An 80-ft Aermotor LS-40 steel lookout built in 1957 near Cedar Grove, Carroll County, Tennessee; manned until the 1970s and now on an active state forestry site.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 standard design; 80-ft bolted steel truss tower with 7 x 7 ft enclosed square cab

access.note: On an active Tennessee Division of Forestry site; no source describes public access. Forestry staff occasionally climb it for maintenance checks.

events.note: Constructed by an unknown entity; Aermotor LS-40 standard design
Constant manning ended in the mid-1970s, when spotter planes and 911 reports replaced lookout watch; the nomination gives no exact year
Modern radio tower about 165 ft north, licensed to the state forestry radio division; the nomination photo is dated ca. 2012
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places as part of the Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933-1975
Registered February 2, 2023 as US 1721, TN 54; site visit January 29, 2023

notes_for_editor: The 1957 build date rests on the NRHP nomination, which cites a 2014 personal communication with the Division's fire management leader; the NHLR entry says build date unknown. Listing date: the nomination gives 11/14/2017; search snippets (TreeAlive, Register Atlas) give Nov 16, 2017; neither was fetched, so the story says only November 2017. Elevation disagrees: 627 ft (NRHP; 191.1 m in the cached tnlandforms GPX) vs 613 ft / 187 m (NHLR); the record's 186.8 m matches the NHLR. The 80-ft height is the overall structure height per the NRHP and NHLR; not confirmed as cab-floor height. The access level 'restricted' is the researcher's reading of 'active TN Forestry site'; no source states public access, so the editor should confirm. The Courier Winter 2018 article (TN Historical Commission) could not be fetched (connection reset). The staffing end date is 'mid-1970s' with no exact year.
